newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Eva HK-Taipei cargo share "as high as" 20pct.
newsitem.headline: Eva HK-Taipei cargo share "as high as" 20pct.

text.p: EVA Air said that its air cargo market share on the new Hong Kong to Taipei route "has been as high as 20 per cent".

The Taiwanese carrier, which began flying on the highly competitive route on August 1, added in a statement it is "quite satisfied" with its performance and the first two months have been as good as expected.
"Both inbound and outbound sectors are being fairly utilised with a favourable cargo yield," the statement said.
EVA rejected earlier comments by Taiwan's flag carrier and rival China Airlines that it was offering unreasonablyy low air cargo prices which were hitting yields.

"The pricing policy that EVA adopts will be decided by the service standard that we provide as well as the market competition. However we are quite proud to say our rate offer in the Hong Kong exporting market has been among the highest," it added.
It said EVA's rate to key agents is around HK$4 per kg unlike a competitor offering rates as low as HK$3.5 per kg.

"We are very happy and satisfied about the market share which has proved all our customers have accepted our service and that's the reason why, even with our 15 per cent capacity among all carriers, our market share has been as high as 20 per cent," the statement added.
EVA's main rivals on the route, China Airlines and Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd, earlier said there has been no significant impact on cargo volumes despite the introduction of 16 EVA flights a week.
These use Boeing 747 Combi aircraft with 45 tons cargo capacity as well as McDonnell Douglas MD-11 and Boeing 767 jets. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
